text: Cytokines fundamentally control memory T-cell differentiation. Following CD8+ T cells from activation to memory generation, common cytokine-receptor γ-chain (γc) family members, notably IL-7 and IL-15, act at every immune-response stage to promote proliferation and survival, propagating a stable, long-lived protective memory pool. Separately, CD4+3− inducer cells closely associate with medullary thymic epithelial cells (mTECs); their RANKL signals drive maturation of RANK-expressing CD80−Aire− mTEC progenitors into CD80+Aire+ mTECs, and RANK-deficient thymic stroma transplanted into immunodeficient hosts induces autoimmunity, revealing a role for CD4+3−RANKL+ cells in intrathymic self-tolerance. Finally, CXCR3, CXCR4 and CXCR7 crosstalk via shared ligands CXCL11 (I-TAC) and CXCL12 (SDF-1). CXCR4 is overexpressed in most human solid tumors and drives metastasis; CXCL12–CXCR4 inhibitors are in preclinical/clinical development, but CXCR7's high-affinity CXCL12 binding and CXCL11 binding challenge selective CXCR4 blockade.
